tasks.short: Advise customers on responsible product use, waste reduction, recycling and disposal.

steps.what: Clarify the product, customer application, location and intended disposal route.
Find current manuals, safety data and supplier recycling instructions.
Assemble relevant instructions and source references into customer guidance.
Check applicability and identify questions requiring specialist advice.
Explain responsible use and disposal, discuss constraints, and refer unresolved questions to specialists.
Record advice, source versions, customer commitments and specialist follow-up.

tasks.design: Configure a product guidance index in the {DOCS}, keyed by product, application, location and document version. A deterministic generator on the {WORKFLOW} assembles approved passages with references; the representative checks applicability before discussing them with the customer. A structured form in the {CRM} captures commitments and routes unresolved questions to a product compliance specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance sits across manuals and supplier documents, with inconsistent product identifiers and version control. Matching it to a customer's actual use still needs judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document metadata, templates and record forms cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the missing lookup and assembly connections; no new reasoning breakthrough is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Contamination, mixed materials and unusual applications can invalidate standard instructions. Keeping location-specific guidance current and securing supplier recycling information remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: The representative uncovers how the customer actually uses the product, explains tradeoffs and recognises when specialist advice is needed.

ambition.what: Product end-of-life planning session before replacement purchases

tasks.altitude: The week contains less document hunting and copying, with more time for customer constraints and follow-up. The representative can propose end-of-life planning sessions; technical and legal approval rights do not expand.

reach.task: Evaluate whether an alternative product reduces waste in the customer's application.
reach.learn: Material compatibility, operating conditions and the evidence needed to compare waste outcomes.

reach.task: Review recurring disposal questions when planning account services.
reach.learn: How to distinguish demand for a useful service from questions requiring specialist escalation.

evidence.claim: Indexed approved documents and deterministic templates can support guidance retrieval and assembly without a model.
Unusual use conditions and disposal routes require human applicability checks and specialist escalation.
The digest reports a chatbot misinformation liability case; it is not evidence of successful disposal-advice automation.

assumptions: The typical company holds product manuals and safety guidance in the {DOCS} and records account activity in the {CRM}.
Most customer communication remains a live conversation, consistent with the supplied time priors.
Machine assembly uses approved passages and explicit applicability fields; it does not infer waste classifications.
Build ranges are estimates for a limited product-family pilot, including access and rollout.
GDPR applies to customer records. EU AI Act obligations apply if AI features are later added.
Employee consultation follows national rules where the implementation changes working practices or introduces monitoring.
unknowns: Which product families have complete, current guidance and reliable identifiers?
Who approves guidance and resolves unusual safety or disposal questions?
Which customer locations and disposal routes must the pilot support?
Can the {DOCS}, {CRM} and {WORKFLOW} exchange records through available interfaces?
What access, retention and employee consultation requirements apply locally?
research_questions: What proportion of questions can be answered using approved passages without interpretation?
Which applicability fields reliably separate standard guidance from cases requiring specialist review?
How often do supplier guidance changes require advice records or customer follow-up to be updated?
new_work: Tag and version approved guidance by product, application and location.
Review assembled guidance before customer communication.
Resolve missing documents and specialist referrals.
Maintain templates, applicability rules and record connections.
Confirm structured conversation records and follow-up tasks.

role.altitude: The representative spends less time finding and copying guidance and more time understanding customer practices. They gain room to propose end-of-life planning services, without gaining specialist approval authority.
reach: Work with sales engineers on waste-reducing product alternatives.
Help sales managers assess demand for end-of-life account services.
skills_to_grow: Capturing customer operating and disposal conditions
role.ambitious_version: Offer a product end-of-life planning session that connects replacement choices, waste reduction and specialist disposal advice.
